description: This repo maintains its OWN toolchain, narrowly. It used to carry `enabled: false` (2026-06-03), which kept Renovate off it entirely — and the cost was measurable: its workflow actions drifted for months with nobody to notice.

The scope is deliberately narrow via `enabledManagers`: only `github-actions` and `npm`, which sees nothing but package.json (the CI validator). `default.json` is the preset that the consumer repos extend UNPINNED from this branch, so main is production for them — it must never be moved by a bot. That holds twice over: no Renovate manager matches `default.json` at all, and `enabledManagers` excludes the `renovate-config` manager that would otherwise match this very file.

Everything is `automerge: false`. The single control is the packageRule below — `platformAutomerge` is NOT a guardrail, it only decides who performs the merge, not whether one happens. Drop that rule and the shared preset's automerge for patch/pin/digest comes back, on a branch that is production for every consumer.

The validator that gates the preset is a devDependency in package.json, installed by CI with `npm ci` from package-lock.json, so its whole tree is pinned by integrity hash. Renovate bumps it through the `npm` manager like any dependency. Until 2026-09-22 it was `npm install -g renovate@<version>` kept current by a regex manager, which pinned renovate but let its transitive tree float on every run. Lock-file maintenance is OFF here: the preset turns it on with automerge, and this branch is production for every consumer; the lockfile moves only with a reviewed renovate bump.

packageRules.description: main is production for every consumer repo: each bump here gets human eyes.
